quizzes.stem: A nightly job always does the same three things in the same order: fetch invoices, ask Claude to label each one, write the labels to a ledger. How should the invoice system be reached?

options.a: As a plain function call made by the code that runs the sequence
options.b: As an MCP server that the model decides to call when it needs invoices
options.c: As a tool in the model's list, left for the model to call when it sees fit
options.d: As a remote agent that the job reaches over an agent-to-agent protocol

explanation.a: The path is fixed, so the code calls the invoice system and the model is not asked whether to.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Workflows are systems where LLMs and tools are orchestrated through predefined code paths", and a fixed step needs no model decision.
explanation.c: Ruled out because for a known path "the code calls, so the step is testable", which a tool left to the model's choice is not.
explanation.d: Ruled out because agent-to-agent suits "The counterpart is another agent with its own goals and owner", and an invoice system is not one.

quizzes.stem: A support agent runs under one service account that may issue refunds, and supervisors legitimately use the same agent for them. A clerk who may only read tickets asks it for a refund, and it is paid. What closes the gap?

options.a: Take the refund tool out of the agent's configuration for every user
options.b: Record each refund so that the clerk's request can be found later
options.c: Allow the call only when the person asking also holds the scope for it
options.d: Add a line to the system prompt telling clerks not to ask for refunds

explanation.c: The call is allowed only when the user holds the scope and the agent does too, so the agent's rights are a ceiling.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "it also stops the supervisors who are allowed to use it".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A record is written after the refund is paid", so it detects and does not prevent.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a line in the system prompt is a request to the model and not a control", and an agent that holds the right can still grant the request.

quizzes.stem: A support agent can read tickets, draft replies, pay customers back and permanently close user profiles. Staff only ever read tickets and draft replies. Applying least privilege, which change reduces risk most?

options.a: Record every repayment and closure so that misuse can be audited later
options.b: Strip the repayment and account-closure capabilities from its configuration altogether
options.c: Keep every capability but ask for a confirmation before each repayment and closure
options.d: Replace the agent with a larger model that follows instructions more reliably

explanation.b: The role never needs those capabilities, so removing them from the configuration removes the risk.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Logging and confirmation prompts are compensating controls", acting after the privilege exists.
explanation.c: is ruled out for the same reason, since a confirmation means "they ask a person to carry the risk of a capability the role never needed".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A larger model does not change what the agent is allowed to do".

quizzes.stem: An internal agent is offered 45 capabilities from eight systems. It increasingly picks the wrong one, and the descriptions of all of them fill much of the window before the first message. Which first step fits?

options.a: Shorten every description so that the definitions take fewer tokens
options.b: Merge the capabilities into a few multi-purpose ones that take a mode argument
options.c: Move to a larger model so that more definitions fit in the window
options.d: Defer most definitions behind a search tool and keep the few most used loaded

explanation.d: With 10 or more tools and large definitions, the search tool loads on demand and the most used tools stay loaded.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "it trades selection quality for tokens" and leaves the tool count where it was.
explanation.b: Ruled out because merging "hides the behaviours from the model's own choice and leaves the number of capabilities the same".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a larger window does not cure it: "Claude's ability to pick the right tool degrades once you exceed 30–50 available tools".

quizzes.stem: A team has 60 tools and turns on the tool search tool. A developer proposes to omit the least-used tools from the request, to save tokens. What does the documentation say?

options.a: Send the least-used ones inside the system prompt as plain text
options.b: Send only the loaded tools, and keep the rest in the application
options.c: Send every definition and mark the infrequent ones as deferred
options.d: Send every definition with a cache breakpoint on each deferred one

explanation.c: The search runs on the full set, so every definition is sent and the infrequent ones are marked as deferred.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "You still send every tool's full definition in the `tools` array on every request".
explanation.a: Ruled out because deferral changes "what enters the context window", and text in the prompt would load them all every time.
explanation.d: Ruled out because deferred tools are kept out of the prefix, and "A deferred tool cannot itself carry a cache breakpoint".

quizzes.stem: A gateway receives a request whose credential has been revoked and which also names a model that the team may not use. What does it answer, and what does it record?

options.a: A refusal for the model, recorded under the team that owned the revoked credential
options.b: A refusal as unauthenticated, logged under unknown with the verdict but no prompt text
options.c: An approval with a warning in the log, since a revoked credential is the provider's concern
options.d: A refusal that keeps the full prompt in the record, so that an attack can be studied later

explanation.b: Who is calling comes first, and the record keeps "the team (or "unknown"), the model and the verdict, and no prompt text".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A request with no credential is refused as unauthenticated even when it also asks for a model it may not have".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "every decision, the refusals included, leaves a record".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a log of content is its own data-protection problem".

quizzes.stem: A partner company's autonomous research system, built on another framework, must hand sub-tasks to your own autonomous system and collect the results. Which mechanism does the integration use?

options.a: An MCP server that exposes your system as one tool of the partner's system
options.b: A direct call from the partner's code into the functions of your system
options.c: A subagent that your own framework starts on the partner's behalf
options.d: An agent-to-agent protocol between the two independent parties

explanation.d: The counterpart is an independent agent with its own owner, which is the agent-to-agent case.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "MCP is for agent-to-tool communication", and the partner's agent is a peer and not a tool.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a direct call suits "The path is known: the same steps in the same order", and a delegation between two agents is not that.
explanation.c: Ruled out because A2A is "Not a sub-agent or tool-call protocol", and a subagent is how an agent delegates inside its own framework, not across two.
